findings.text: A swap device must prove liveness through its users reference before any other device field or flag may be examined, with a read barrier separating the liveness check from later reads to pair with setup and teardown ordering.

Slow allocation walks the available-device priority collection with rotation so each visit moves the visited device to the back, dropping the collection lock while attempting liveness and slot allocation on one device, then rechecking whether the saved successor is still linked and restarting from the head when it has left, exiting early once cache insertion succeeds or the target is large.

Requested allocation order follows the folio size when a folio is supplied and zero otherwise, and any nonzero order request against a device that is not block backed fails immediately without scanning.

Rotational devices serialize allocation through a per-device global lock and first retry a remembered global hint for the requested order after verifying usability, treating an empty hint as a request to start at the owning cluster boundary before scanning that cluster.

When the hint misses or the device is solid state, selection prefers discard-aware free space, then same-order partially used space, then free space when discard is absent, then reclamation of full space under global pressure, then a single same-order fragmented cluster, with order zero finally stealing from higher-order fragmented and partially used space while nonzero orders stop after the fragmented attempt.

List scanning isolates and locks at most one cluster per attempt, returning its scan result when productive and repeating across further entries only when the caller asks for a full sweep, otherwise stopping after one cluster.

Cluster isolation runs under the device lock, try-locking entries in order until one succeeds, detaching it and resetting its state to detached while remembering the prior state, then releasing the device lock; clusters detached from the free collection must have their tables brought up before use and only a small set of prior states is considered valid.

Table bring-up for a detached free cluster first tries an allocation that cannot sleep while holding local, global when rotational, and cluster locks, and on failure releases all locks for a sleepable attempt before reacquiring them on the possibly new processor, returning the cluster to the free collection and reporting absence when the second attempt also fails.

Table creation requires an empty detached cluster and is a no-op when a table is already visible, otherwise installs a zeroed backing object plus optional accounting and zero tracking structures, tearing everything down and reporting resource exhaustion when any piece cannot be obtained.

Reclamation of full clusters examines a single cluster by default and scales the quota with device usage when forced, dropping the cluster lock to attempt reclaim of folio entries with no remaining references and advancing past reclaimed extents, relocating clusters that yielded nothing, and yielding the processor only in forced sweeps.

Synchronous discard walks the active-device priority collection with lock drops around per-device work, invoking scheduled discard only on devices advertising page discard, stopping at the first device that makes progress and restarting from the head when the saved successor has left the collection.

Per-device scheduled discard repeatedly unlinks the first discard-pending cluster while keeping its discard mark, releases the device lock to discard the whole cluster range, then under the cluster lock clears the mark and returns the cluster to the allocation pool, reporting whether any cluster was processed.

Discard of a cluster range resolves each page offset through an ordered extent tree keyed by start page, slices the request at extent boundaries, translates pages to sector units, issues discards without sleeping in filesystem context, advances through successors, halts on first issuance failure, and treats an uncovered offset as fatal.
Freeing swap for a folio succeeds only when the folio is eligible for cache release and has no remaining swap references, in which case it dissociates the cache entry and marks the folio dirty.

Testing whether a folio may still be referenced requires the folio to be locked and present in swap cache, then inspects reference counts for every page covered by the folio under read-side protection, relying on the folio lock rather than additional cluster locking to keep entries stable.

Reclaim writeout keeps folios with unexpected references or no owning mapping, reactivates folios that are neither shared-memory nor anonymous, requires successful transition from dirty to under-write state, routes shared-memory and anonymous folios to different writers with possible splitting of large shared-memory folios back to the caller list, translates writer outcomes into keep, activate, clean or success, and accounts completed writes.

Whether throttling is considered sane depends on build options, with one variant always reporting sane and another reporting sane outside cgroup reclaim or when the memory controller uses the default hierarchy.

Clearing dirty state for input-output requires a locked folio and, for mappings that support writeback, synchronizes against concurrent faults by cleaning processor dirty tracking then re-dirtying through the filesystem before atomically clearing the folio dirty mark and adjusting dirty, reclaimable, pending and donotcache counters only when the mark was present.

Swap writeout proceeds through freeable short-circuit, architecture preparation, zero-content detection with zero marking, clearing of stale zero marks, compressed backing attempt with accounting, hierarchy-wide writeback permission check, and finally asynchronous page submission, unlocking on all early exits while leaving the folio locked across submission and re-dirtying or reactivating on defined failures.

Zero detection maps each constituent page locally and tests the trailing word before the leading words for early rejection, while zero marks are applied or cleared for every page of a locked swapcache folio under the owning cluster lock with global and object-group event accounting.

Deriving and locking the cluster for a folio requires a locked swapcache folio and resolves the owning device and offset from the stored swap entry, while an alternate build provides no cluster support and always reports absence.

Several paths assume list stability across lock drops and must restart when a successor disappears, missing extent coverage is treated as unrecoverable, concurrent discard and relocation rely on a retained discard mark, and sleepable table allocation may resume on a different processor while continuing with the previously isolated cluster.

Folio and writeback helpers for freeing swap, clearing dirty state, performing swap writeout, querying hierarchy writeback permission, querying compressed-cache enablement, and obtaining a referenced object group are visible beyond their defining files.

A swap device logically tracks liveness references, capability flags, global allocation hints with their lock, device and cluster locks, usage counters, size limits, backing extents and block device, plus separate collections for free, same-order partially used, fragmented, full and discard-pending clusters.

A cluster logically tracks list linkage, a lock, state flags, a reference-count table with optional accounting and zero tracking, while an extent tracks a page interval, a backing block start, and tree linkage ordered by start page.
Zero marking for a single slot uses either a flag stored alongside the count after verifying countability or a separate bitmap updated under the cluster lock, depending on build configuration.
